_comment: A luminance relief (chopshop-bp#3), and the whole input the feature needs:
one contour per traced tonal region, each carrying the `luminance` the
CALLER measured from the raster it traced. The `relief` block is the rule;
the per-element numbers are the measurement; nothing here is computed by
this repository, which draws documents and does not measure them.
The subject is a face, because a portrait bas-relief is the thing a
height-from-luminance rule was invented for: the nose (0.97) is the
highest plane, the eye sockets (0.18) among the deepest, and the whole form
is carried by tonal order rather than by outline. The background sits at
0.10 and the face at 0.62, so the head reads as a plane standing off a
The same document with the `relief` block removed and every element at z=0
draws as a flat image -- which is what the render test compares against,
because a rule that validated, resolved and was then dropped still renders
a perfectly valid picture of a flat drawing.
